newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault shares race ahead on change in sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Renault shares race ahead on change in sentiment.

text.p: Shares in Renault surged to a year high on Wednesday, bolstered by a stream of analysts' recommendations that marked a major change in sentiment surrounding the stock.
Brokers said the winding down of the Vilvoorde saga, with the Belgian plant workers' overwhelming approval for a redundancy deal offered by the company, also helped the share.
The stock was up 9.83 percent at 181 francs ($29.35) at 1355 GMT after having been briefly suspended limit-up. It surged far ahead of the CAC-40 index that was 3.35 percent higher.
It rose 5.98 percent on Tuesday after JP Morgan raised its rating to a buy.

Also on Tuesday, workers at the Vilvoorde plant voted 92 percent to accept a redundancy deal offered by Renault. Analysts say the conclusion of the painful chapter signals that a company restructuring announced in the spring will proceed.

Its stock has risen 59 percent since the start of the year and is finally above the price at which it was offered during the first leg of the company's privatisation in late 1994. Institutional investors paid 176 francs for their shares while retail investors paid 165 francs.

Paribas Capital Markets analyst Francois Colli raised his rating on Renault's stock on Wednesday to buy from hold, after concluding it was undervalued compared with such competitors as Fiat and Volkswagen.
He said his recommendation was based on the restructuring, the success of the Megane Scenic car and the beneficial impact of the British pound's rise on Renault's results.
Colli expects the group to turn a profit this year after losing 5.25 billion francs in 1996, including 3.91 billion francs of restructuring provisions.
"We've been through the worst with Renault. The news will be good from here on," said Societe Generale analyst Philippe Barrier, who agrees that the share is undervalued.
Salomon Brothers analyst John Lawson triggered buying last week when he raised his rating on the stock to buy from hold.
